quarterly_data.signal: 10-K fiscal 2025 results (in thousands): total revenue $812,033 versus $412,260 in 2024, up 97.0%; income from operations $45,113 versus a loss of $(257,122); net loss $(68,088) versus $(281,890). The $417,604 thousand rise in molecular profiling services revenue breaks down as MI Profile volume increase $51,979, MI Profile ASP increase due to solution and payer mix $311,383, and Caris Assure for therapy selection volume and ASP increase $54,242. Net cash provided by operating activities was $83,155, purchases of property and equipment $16,260 (2024: $8,444) and free cash flow $66,895.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue $812,033 thousand (+97.0%); income from operations $45,113 thousand; free cash flow $66,895 thousand; capex $16,260 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K supply commitments: Caris enters into various supply agreements that contain purchase commitments, most based on a binding forecast for an agreed-upon period of 12 months or less; future minimum purchase commitments under such agreements were $7.6 million, all due in 2026, and supplies purchased under such agreements totalled $30.0 million in 2025 and $32.3 million in 2024. The 10-K also describes the July 2024 master supply agreement with Roche Diagnostics Corporation for sequencing probes and other testing supplies and equipment, under which rolling forecasts currently become three- and six-month binding purchase commitments for catalog and custom products.
quarterly_data.figure: minimum purchase commitments $7.6 million (due 2026); supplies purchased $30.0 million (2025) vs $32.3 million (2024)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: the transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations for contracts with an original expected duration over one year was $6.5 million as of December 31, 2025, expected to be recognized within twelve months; contract liabilities were $24,492 thousand (December 31, 2024: $7,470 thousand).

10-K: Caris names Moderna, AbbVie, Xencor, Merck KGaA and Genentech as biopharma partners to which its molecular profiling solutions and multi-omic data provide value, and says it has achieved external validation of its Caris Discovery approach through strategic partnerships with established biopharma companies such as Genentech, Merck KGaA and Xencor to develop therapeutics against novel targets that emanate from its molecular insights; the Caris Discovery partnerships are designed to emphasize both near term revenue and the potential upside of successful therapeutics. Caris has also entered agreements with clinical data partners such as ConcertAI, Flatiron and COTA to create matched clinico-genomic datasets that can be licensed to biopharma companies for drug discovery.

connects_to.relationship: licence of Caris molecular profiling datasets for drug discovery

contracts.signal: 10-K: Caris and its partners have entered into agreements with AbbVie, Moderna and others to license Caris datasets for use in drug discovery; Moderna is also named among the biopharma partners to which Caris's molecular profiling solutions and multi-omic data provide value.

players.product: NovaSeq sequencing, BioInsight, and Billion Cell Atlas multi-omics data

connects_to.relationship: sole supplier of NGS sequencing instruments, sequencing reagent kits and instrument maintenance

contracts.signal: 10-K supplier disclosure: Caris relies on Illumina as the sole supplier of NGS instruments and the associated sequencing reagent kits for its solutions, and as the sole provider of maintenance and repair services for these instruments. Caris entered Illumina's 'open offer' supply agreement in November 2022; it has no minimum purchase requirements but provides volume discounts and other promotions, is irrevocable by Illumina until its expiration in August 2033, and Caris may terminate it on 90 days' prior written notice.
contracts.units: sole supplier of NGS instruments and sequencing reagent kits

connects_to.relationship: AWS cloud hosting and data analysis

contracts.signal: 10-K supplier disclosure: Caris hosts its data on, and conducts certain data analysis through, Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud-based hosting facilities as well as its own co-located or on-premise computing infrastructure, and cites the October 2025 AWS outage as an example of the technical problems or outages that could disrupt its operations or data processing.
